rows.grounds: genitive of the subject whose manifestability is denied

items.question: Can unreal things manifest the seeing-speech whose nature is true?
premises: Seeing-speech possesses a true nature.
Unreal things lack the capacity to manifest what is truly real.
items.inference: Unreal things cannot manifest seeing-speech.
items.plain_english: And the seeing-speech, whose nature is true, cannot be manifested by unreal things.

rows.grounds: passive action of being proven or made known

items.question: By what means of knowledge can that seeing-speech be established?
premises: Establishing something requires a valid means of knowledge.
No valid means of knowledge for seeing-speech has been identified.
items.inference: Seeing-speech cannot be established by any available means of knowledge.
items.plain_english: Or by what means of knowledge is that seeing-speech established?

rows.grounds: one lacking direct experience or authority
capacity to speak of what is not experienced

items.question: Can an unreliable person speak authoritatively about an unexperienced object?
premises: You yourselves deny that an unreliable person can speak of unexperienced objects.
Speaking of seeing-speech without direct access would require such speaking.
items.inference: The opponent cannot consistently claim to establish seeing-speech.
items.plain_english: For you yourselves hold that one who is not reliable cannot speak of an object not experienced.

rows.grounds: another subject to whom seeing-speech becomes object

items.question: Does seeing-speech become an object for another cognizing subject?
premises: If seeing-speech is established by another, it becomes that other's object.
Becoming an object contradicts its nature as self-luminous seeing.
items.inference: Seeing-speech cannot be made an object for another without contradiction.
items.plain_english: Thus, then, that seeing-speech would become an object for another.

rows.grounds: refers to inference as a valid means for opponent

items.question: Can intuition establish seeing-speech as a valid means for the opponent?
premises: Intuition might be proposed as the means to know seeing-speech.
Intuition is not inference, and inference is not accepted by you here.
items.inference: Intuition cannot serve as a valid means of knowledge for the opponent.
items.plain_english: Or if intuition is proposed, that is not inference, and inference is not valid for you.

items.question: Can seeing-speech apprehend itself by its own self?
premises: One might propose that seeing-speech sees itself by itself.
Self-apprehension would require a distinction between seer and seen.
items.inference: The proposal of self-apprehension raises a further difficulty.
items.plain_english: Now if that seeing-speech will apprehend itself by its own self—

rows.grounds: extends the question to that self-seeing
the seeing-speech as object of seeing
imperative directing attention to the problem
relative referring to the seeing instance

items.question: What sees the seeing-speech when it is said to see itself?
premises: If seeing-speech sees itself, that seeing must itself be accounted for.
A further seer would be required to see the seeing-speech.
items.inference: Self-seeing leads to an unresolved regress or contradiction.
items.plain_english: Then it must indeed be explained: see, what itself sees that seeing-speech?

rows.grounds: that which is to be proven

items.question: Can an unreal establisher prove an unreal object in this framework?
premises: In this view the object to be established is unreal.
The agent that establishes it is also unreal.
items.inference: Neither the object nor the establisher has reality in this framework.
items.plain_english: In this view, what is to be established is unreal, and the establisher is unreal.

rows.grounds: refers to seeing-speech or its reality
is made to stand as real
truth or reality of that means

items.question: What guarantees the reality of the means used to establish seeing-speech?
premises: Any means used to establish seeing-speech must itself be real.
The reality of that means has not been demonstrated.
items.inference: The proposed means of establishment lacks guaranteed reality.
items.plain_english: Or by what means of knowledge is it established, and what is the reality of that means?

rows.grounds: source claimed to produce merit or result
attainment of heaven and similar results

items.question: Who gains connection with heaven from the utterance of correct words?
premises: Correct word utterance is claimed to yield results like heaven.
If the underlying speech principle is unreal, the beneficiary is unclear.
items.inference: The claimed fruit of correct utterance becomes untenable.
items.plain_english: For whom is there connection with heaven and such results from the utterance of correct words?

rows.grounds: levels of speech beginning with middle

items.question: What enjoyment can inert and variegated middle speech and others provide?
premises: Middle speech and related levels are treated as inert and variegated.
Inert entities cannot be subjects of genuine enjoyment.
items.inference: Attributing enjoyment to inert levels of speech is incoherent.
items.plain_english: What enjoyment can there be for inert middle speech and the rest, with their variegated nature?

items.question: Does the opponent's position lead to the annihilation of grammar?
premises: The opponent's account undermines the reality of speech.
Grammar depends on the reality and functioning of speech.
items.inference: The opponent's position entails the annihilation of grammar.
items.plain_english: Thus, for you, even grammar comes to be annihilated.

rows.grounds: that which has been cut off

items.question: Should a view that annihilates grammar be abandoned as untenable?
premises: A position that annihilates grammar is self-undermining.
Self-undermining positions should be abandoned.
items.inference: Such a position should indeed be abandoned.
items.plain_english: What is thus annihilated would indeed have to be abandoned.

rows.grounds: something not pertinent to the topic

items.question: Have the opponents stated only irrelevant matters in this discussion?
premises: The opponents' claims fail to address the core issue.
Irrelevant statements do not establish the point at stake.
items.inference: The opponents' statements are not merely irrelevant but also ineffective.
uncertainties: Scope of 'not only' is compressed in the verse
items.plain_english: Not only has irrelevant matter been stated here by you.

rows.grounds: refers to the subject or self

items.question: Is self-experience apprehended only within present time?
premises: The opponent may claim self-experience is apprehended in present time.
Temporal limitation raises questions about the nature of that experience.
items.inference: Framing self-experience as temporally limited is problematic.
items.plain_english: This one's own experience is apprehended in present time.

rows.grounds: the self as subject of experience

items.question: How can the infinite self be experienced without any limitation?
premises: Experience ordinarily involves limitation or delimitation.
The self is claimed to be infinite.
items.inference: Experiencing the infinite self without limitation is conceptually problematic for the opponent.
items.plain_english: What experience of the infinite self is possible without limitation?

rows.grounds: a means of knowledge that is not all-pervading

items.question: Can consciousness possess a limited form known by a non-all-pervading means?
premises: A non-all-pervading means of knowledge apprehends limited forms.
Consciousness is not observed to have such a limited form.
items.inference: Consciousness cannot be grasped as a limited form by a limited means.
items.plain_english: Indeed, a form of consciousness is not observed through a means of knowledge that is not all-pervading.

items.question: How can there be forms of consciousness if consciousness lacks material hardness?
premises: Consciousness does not become a material quality like hardness.
Material forms presuppose such qualities.
items.inference: Positing forms of consciousness as material forms is incoherent.
items.plain_english: Consciousness does not become hardness; so how, then, can there be forms of consciousness?

rows.grounds: emphatic reference to the same principle

items.question: Does appeal to a beginningless word-principle establish equality with the opponent's view?
premises: The opponent may claim parity by invoking a beginningless word-principle.
Mere beginninglessness does not resolve the stated defects.
items.inference: Invoking a beginningless word-principle does not establish equality.
items.plain_english: Now, is there equality by appeal to that very beginningless word-principle?

rows.grounds: defects such as absence of valid means

items.question: Does a sphoṭa-based word-principle escape faults like absence of valid means?
premises: The word-principle may be conceived as sphoṭa.
Faults such as lack of valid means still apply.
items.inference: A sphoṭa-based account remains subject to the same faults.
items.plain_english: Or is there faultiness, such as the absence of means of knowledge, even for what is of the nature of sphoṭa?

items.question: Can an eternal word-principle be manifested by transient sounds?
premises: The word-principle is claimed to be eternal.
Manifestation by sounds would imply dependence on transient factors.
items.inference: An eternal word-principle cannot be manifested by sounds in this way.
items.plain_english: And if the word-principle is eternal, it cannot be manifested by sounds.

items.question: Does the same reasoning not apply equally within the opponent's own view?
premises: The opponent raises objections against the proposed account.
The same logical difficulties apply to the opponent's own position.
items.inference: The opponent's view is subject to the same reasoning.
items.plain_english: O Śiva, does not this same reasoning apply in your view as well?

items.question: Why should one desist from equating the opponent's view with the true position?
premises: The true position is grounded in reality.
Because of this reality, there is no equality with the opponent's view.
items.inference: One should desist from the opponent's mistaken position.
items.plain_english: And because of its reality there is no equality; therefore one should desist from this.

rows.grounds: by a figurative mode of expression
due to designation in feminine gender

items.question: Why is the power of knowledge designated figuratively with feminine gender?
premises: The power of knowledge is spoken of in feminine gender.
Such designation is figurative rather than literal.
items.inference: The feminine designation of knowledge-power is a figurative usage.
items.plain_english: The power of knowledge is remembered figuratively, by designation in the feminine gender.
